name: Adisa Handwoven Pullover
description:
Made by Adisa Okonkwo-Brennan, a single artisan working out of a fourth-floor studio in the Tier 3 Havenwood district, these pullovers are woven on a traditional floor loom using a blend of West African kente strip-weaving technique and Nordic colorwork structure. Each pullover is assembled from strips of hand-woven fabric joined in a way that makes the seams a design element rather than a flaw. The color combinations are Adisa's own — warm golds and deep indigos alongside unexpected interventions of forest green or rust. No two are identical. The fabric is a wool-linen blend that has a pleasant roughness when new and breaks in to something close to linen-soft over time.

Adisa sells through a small waiting list and occasionally through a Tier 3 design collective market. Prices are firm and non-negotiable. The pullovers have found their way onto people across tiers — Tier 2 buyers who saved for months, Tier 4 buyers who appreciate the provenance, and one documented Tier 5 Spire resident who keeps it as their 'real clothes' for private evenings. Adisa doesn't care who buys them as long as the list stays moving.
what_it_says: You found something real. Whether you saved for six months or bought it without looking at the price, you recognize craft when you see it — and you wanted to be close to something made by a person.
story_hooks: Adisa has been approached by a Tier 4 corponation wanting to license the weaving pattern for a mass-production run — the offer is large enough to change their life, and the refusal has made some corporate representatives persistent in ways that are starting to feel like pressure.
One of Adisa's pullovers was worn by a person who disappeared — and a character is trying to trace the owner's last movements through the waiting list records.
The wool-linen blend Adisa sources comes from a supplier with an unusual background, and a character investigating something unrelated stumbles across the supply chain.
